chapter: Chicago, Villa Venice and Louis Armstrong
title: Rehearsing with Milt Hinton; Tick Gray's roadhouse group
summary: Budd and Hinton rehearse daily and play a roadhouse with Tick Gray; Hinton's mother refuses to let him go to Milwaukee.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Oh, and incidentally, ladies and gentlemen, during those years I met Milt Hinton, and we used to rehearse every day. We would get together and have our little sessions every day. Finally, one day -- what was Tick's real name?
Tick Grey, got a little group together, and we went out to like a roadhouse type thing, and --
Bill Bottoms. Where was that, Blue Island?
It was way out of town. Another roadhouse.
Way out of town, yeah, and we had our -- we had a good little group. But Everett Barksdale was in Chicago at that time, and --
Budd, you were writing, I can remember every --
Well I was in my formative stage of trying to write then, you know.
Sure was, and it was so beautiful.
And Milt, Milt was playing, man. I never for -- now we can tell the story, can't we?

Like I had a little job in Milwaukee, and I wanted Milt to go, and he asked his mother, and she turned left on him, and he fell down on the floor, beating his fists and kicking his legs and crying "I want to go!" She said, "You're going to stay here and finish school."
She said no. She still said that.
